name: sync_basic
kind: survey: the mbarrier hand-off between two warps measured with clocks (blocked try_wait against how long it had been blocked, the hint form, a try_wait issued after another warp's arrive), and bar.sync with a late arrival, at 32 warps and with two CTAs on an SM; installs nothing
why: Version 3 (data_seen (d), (e)) found that the two-warp numbers in hand do not isolate the hand-off: the ping-pong period is one warp's own loop (YIELD in front of its try_wait) and bounds the hand-off at about 42 cycles for a waiter blocked about 60 cycles, while the installed values (release 87.9, suspended wake 228 / 146, NANOSLEEP.SYNCS wake 136 / 72) come from compiled probes whose windows hold a YIELD, a poll loop and 64-bit clock reads. Full-GPU kernels wait for hundreds to thousands of cycles in try_wait (with and without the suspend hint) before the phase completes, so the value is needed against the time the waiter has been blocked. For bar.sync the cells with every warp arriving together grow by 2 cycles per warp, the earlier late-arrival probe was flat: the rule (service of arrivals one at a time, or a release latency that grows with the participants) depends on a late-arrival cell in a hand-written kernel.
data_seen_before_freezing: sync_basic v1 / v2 addenda and tables, version 3's reading of them, the source records barrier_release / trywait_wake / nanosleep (v2r1). No data from the cells below.

probe.chain: as versions 1 / 2 (hand-written PTX, pass-through build, loop gate with the listing recorded next to the cubin, direct runs with value checks, then capture, two sampling passes, replay with engine build 74ce8aab). Parameters: out, n (iterations, 64), k (trips of the delay loop). Per thread six words: t0, t1, check (iterations done), check2 (false try_wait results), sum_a, sum_b, the last two being sums over the iterations of %clock values read at the places named per cell (32-bit, wrapping; only differences of sums are used).
probe.delay: a counted loop of k trips whose bound is the parameter k and whose body is one dependent add; its length in cycles is not assumed, it is read from the cell (period and sums).

cells.u.selfpair: one warp per CTA, own barrier (count 1). Per iteration: ca = %clock; arrive (lane 0); try_wait on the phase just completed, in a retry loop; cw = %clock as the first instruction after the try_wait is true; parity toggled. sum_a = sum ca, sum_b = sum cw. The reference for 'an arrive followed by a ready try_wait' with exactly the clock placement of the hand-off cells.
cells.u.selfwait: as u.selfpair with the first clock read between the arrive and the try_wait (cb): sum_a = sum cb. The reference for u.ready.
cells.u.handoff: two warps per CTA (leader, follower), barriers A and B (count 1). Leader per iteration: delay(k); ca = %clock; arrive A; try_wait B in a retry loop; cw = %clock. Follower per iteration: try_wait A in a retry loop; cw = %clock; delay(k); ca = %clock; arrive B. Each warp: sum_a = sum ca, sum_b = sum cw. Each try_wait is issued right after the warp's own arrive and is blocked for about one delay before the other warp arrives. k = 0, 16, 64, 256, 512, 1024 (the last is meant to cross the 1.96 microsecond time-out: check2 then counts the false results).
cells.u.handoff_hint: u.handoff with the try_wait carrying suspendTimeHint 10000000 ns (the value of the full-GPU kernels, 0x989680); k = 0, 64, 256, 1024. The SASS form (NANOSLEEP.SYNCS or other) is recorded by the gate.
cells.u.ready: two warps per CTA. Leader per iteration: arrive A; try_wait B in a retry loop. Follower per iteration: delay(k); cb = %clock; try_wait A in a retry loop; cw = %clock; arrive B. Follower: sum_a = sum cb, sum_b = sum cw. The follower's try_wait is issued one delay after the leader's arrive. k = 64.
cells.u.bar_late: W warps per CTA; warp 0 runs delay(k) before each bar.sync 0, the others go straight to it. Every warp: cb = %clock before the bar.sync, ca = %clock after it; sum_a = sum cb, sum_b = sum ca. W = 1, 4, 16; k = 64.
cells.u.bar: version 1's s.bar at 2, 8 and 32 warps per CTA (2 and 8 had clocks only), and at 4 warps with a grid of twice the SM count (two CTAs per SM; the placement is taken from the capture, a cell with one CTA per SM is reported as unrealised).

probe.gate: per cell the loop listing must contain the SYNCS / BAR instructions named for it; for the pairs (u.selfpair, u.handoff) and (u.selfwait, u.ready) the instructions between the clock read and the arrive / try_wait, and between the try_wait and the clock read after it, are listed side by side; if they differ the difference in issue cycles is stated from the listing and the comparison carries that uncertainty.

derivation.clock: direct runs, launch 0 and launch 2, per CTA then median over CTAs. Period = (t1 - t0) / n per warp. Hand-off cells, per direction: X = (sum cw of the waiter - sum ca of the arriver, mod 2^32) / n, the mean cycles from the clock read in front of the arrive to the clock read behind the try_wait it completes. u.selfpair: X_self = (sum cw - sum ca) / n; u.selfwait and u.ready: Y = (sum cw - sum cb) / n; u.bar_late: Z = (sum ca - sum cb) / n per warp. Blocked time of a waiter before the completing arrive = period / 2 (its try_wait is issued right after its own arrive, half a period before the other warp's; exact to the few instructions between a warp's arrive and its try_wait). Values are usable when check = n in every warp and X is the same within 3 cycles over the CTAs of a launch (both warps of a CTA read the same SM clock).
derivation.samples: per pc by class next to the replay's reasons, as versions 1 / 2 (where the blocked warp is booked; what the YIELD and the retry loop cost).
derivation.usable: clock readings from rows with right check words; sampling rows with at least 2000 samples in both passes.

questions_before_data.hand-off: X(k) - X_self against the blocked time, both directions. P1: within 5 cycles of 0 at every k below the time-out: a blocked try_wait returns one result latency after the completing arrive, there is no wake cost. P2: a constant above 5: a fixed wake cost (the value). P3: grows or steps with the blocked time: the table, and the blocked time at which it changes. The k that crosses the time-out is reported separately (false results per iteration, X).
questions_before_data.hint: the same readings for the hint form, and whether its listing and its booking differ from the plain form (NANOSLEEP.SYNCS, class sleeping).
questions_before_data.ready: Y_ready - Y_self. Q1: within 3 cycles of 0: another warp's completed phase is visible at once (no release latency). Q2: larger: that difference is the release latency between warps.
questions_before_data.bar late: Z of the late warp at W = 1, 4, 16. Z1: grows by about 2 cycles per warp (as with simultaneous arrival): a release latency that depends on the participants. Z2: flat at the one-warp value: arrivals are served one at a time and the early ones were served long before. Otherwise reported.
questions_before_data.bar shapes: cost per barrier at 2, 8 and 32 warps against 7.5 + 2.0 per warp; with two CTAs per SM: as one CTA of 4 warps (service per CTA) or as 8 warps (service per SM).
questions_before_data.replay: per cell replay against hardware as before; nothing is judged.

install: Nothing is installed from this version. The installation of the hand-off and of bar.sync is a later version whose rule is written after these readings.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case.

addenda.when: 2026-11-16, before any probe was built or run
addenda.text: Frame detail: eight words per thread instead of six (t0, t1, check, check2, sum_a, sum_b, acc, 0); acc is the running value of the delay loop's dependent add, stored so that ptxas keeps the loop. Nothing else changes.

addenda.when: 2026-11-17, h100 and b300 runs (20 cells each; every gate passed, check words right; data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sync_basic-v4/{h100,b300}, clock table derive_v4-<device>.txt, per-pc table derive-<device>.txt, listings side by side gate-sidebyside.txt; replay with engine build 74ce8aab; b300 replays of the four u.bar cells still running when this was written, their hardware columns are complete) — readings; nothing installed
addenda.text: HAND-OFF (plain try_wait). X from the clock read in front of the arrive to the clock read behind the try_wait it completes: 61 (leader's arrive, clock read 2 instructions in front of it) and 63 (follower's arrive, 4 instructions in front) at every k on both devices, to the cycle, for a waiter blocked 140 to 9500 cycles (period / 2), and unchanged at k = 1024 where the 1.96 microsecond time-out is crossed (one false result per iteration, the retried try_wait blocks again). X_B - X_A = 2 = the difference in instructions between clock read and arrive, so the two clock reads sample at the same point of their issue and X - (instructions to the arrive) = 59 is arrive issue -> issue of the waiter's clock read. The waiter's path from the reader of the predicate to that clock read (BRA, BSYNC, S2UR) holds 19.9-20.4 cycles by the samples (BSYNC waits 5, the S2UR behind it 12), so arrive issue -> the blocked waiter's reader issues = 38.6 / 38.8 (h100), 39.1 / 38.9 (b300): the SYNCS.PHASECHK result latency (issue -> reader 37.8 in u.selfpair) plus one cycle. There is no wake cost and no dependence on the blocked time. MY REFERENCE CELL WAS WRONG for the comparison the protocol named: X_self (159 / 160.5) holds what a hand-off does not, namely the YIELD that ptxas puts in front of the try_wait (about 50 cycles at the TRYWAIT pc before it issues), the try_wait's own issue-to-result (37) and the first reader of the S2UR (29); the pcs of u.selfpair sum to 157. So none of P1 / P2 / P3 can be read off X - X_self; read by listing and samples instead, the substance is P1. READY: Y_ready 152 on both devices against Y_self 153 (h100) / 155 (b300), same instructions in the window: a try_wait issued after another warp's arrive returns as after the warp's own (Q1): there is no release latency between warps. HINT form (suspendTimeHint 10 ms): listing = SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT, then @!P NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680, @!P SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64 (no TRYWAIT), @!P add, @!P BRA back to the NANOSLEEP; no YIELD. X = 91 / 93 at every k on both devices, 30 more than plain. Below the time-out the first TRYWAIT blocks until the arrive exactly as without the hint (the whole wait is long_scoreboard on the NANOSLEEP.SYNCS, which is the reader of the predicate, then predicated off); the 30 extra cycles are instructions: the predicated-off NANOSLEEP and PHASECHK and 22 cycles of long_scoreboard on the reader of the predicated-off PHASECHK. At k = 1024 (time-out crossed, the loop runs about two passes and the warp does sleep) X is the same 91 / 93; the sleep is booked long_scoreboard at the NANOSLEEP.SYNCS pc, not class sleeping; the wake latency of the sleep by itself is not isolated (the passes are not separable by pc), only that sleeping adds nothing to the total. Installed values this contradicts: release 87.9 + result 37.9 for a wait issued after another warp's arrive (hardware 38), suspended wake 228 / 146 + 37.9 for a blocked waiter (hardware 39), release + NANOSLEEP.SYNCS wake 224 / 160-224 (hardware: nothing beyond the instruction path). Replay 74ce8aab of u.handoff.k0 / u.handoff_hint.k0: 420.6 / 427.3 cycles per iteration against hardware 277.5 / 336.8 (h100). BAR LATE: Z is not usable. BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING does not hold the instructions right behind it: the clock read after the bar.sync issues before the warp blocks (Z = 6 in every warp, early ones included), and class barrier sits on the third instruction after the BAR (an LDC), not on the next one as in s.bar. Read from periods instead (the late warp's loop): h100 753.2 / 753.1 / 787.0 at W = 1 / 4 / 16, b300 723.9 / 726.9 / 742.7 (sample totals 747.6 / 748.0 / 780.7 and 719.1 / 724.7 / 739.9): with 4 warps a late arrival costs what one warp costs on h100 (+0.4) and 6 more on b300; with 16 warps +33 (h100) / +21 (b300). Neither Z1 (+6 at 4 warps, +30 at 16) nor Z2 (flat) fits both shapes; candidates not separated by these cells: the released warps are woken one after another with the late one not first, or the late warp's delay loop loses issue slots to the three warps that share its SMSP after the release (not_selected is present at 16 warps). BAR SHAPES (sample totals minus the loop frame 5.86, all warps arriving together): 2 / 8 / 32 warps 11.3 / 23.4 / 69.9 (h100), 11.7 / 23.3 / 70.7 (b300) against 7.5 + 2.0 per warp = 11.5 / 23.5 / 71.5: the law holds to 32 warps (at 32 part of it is mio_throttle 7 and not_selected 4). Two CTAs of 4 warps on one SM (placement confirmed, 132 x 2): 15.5 / 15.7, the value of one such CTA (15.6): the cost is per CTA, not per SM. Replay: 16.5-27 flat. bar.sync stays uninstalled: the simultaneous law is established, what a late arrival costs at more than one warp per SMSP is not.
